newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Carulla sees '97 net up 37 pct.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Carulla sees '97 net up 37 pct.

text.p: The head of Carulla y Compania, one of Colombia's five largest retail chains, said Tuesday he was aiming for a 37 percent growth in company profits by the end of the year.
Despite the recession of the Colombian economy,company chairman Jorge Carulla forecast the supermarket chain's sales would grow by 30 percent in 1997.

"We're going to see if we can maintain our position," Carulla told Reuters in an interview. "We're adjusting to the current recession ... we've cut prices and have seen a significant increase in volume," he added.
The Colombian economy is considered to be in recession after registering two consecutive quarters of negative growth in gross domestic product,

The Carulla chain posted 39 percent growth in 1997 Q1 net profits, up to 1.77 billion pesos compared to 1.27 billion pesos in the same period in 1996. Net profits for all of 1996 were 5.4 billion pesos.
